question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 18 hours, pipe B can fill the same tank in 30 hours and pipe C can fill the same tank in 18 hours. The time taken by them to fill the same tank if they operate together is::
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Capacity = LCM(18, 30, 18) = 90 units.

Combined efficiency = (90 ÷ 18) + (90 ÷ 30) + (90 ÷ 18) = 5 + 3 + 5 = 13 units/hour.

Total time taken = Total Capacity ÷ Combined efficiency = 90 ÷ 13 = 6¹²/₁₃ hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 6¹²/₁₃ hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Pipe A fills the tank in 18 hours.

Pipe B fills the tank in 30 hours.

Pipe C fills the tank in 18 hours.

**Formula Used:**

Time = Total Work ÷ Total Efficiency

 
 

 **Pipe**
 **Hours**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A
 18

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total efficiency of A, B, and C = 5 + 3 + 5 = 13 units/hour.

⇒ Time taken to fill the tank = 90 ÷ 13

⇒ Time taken = 6¹²/₁₃ hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 6¹²/₁₃ hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns Work Logic

The logic for Pipes and Cisterns is identical to Time and Work. The total capacity of the cistern is considered as the total work (usually the LCM of the given individual times).

Leakage or Emptying Pipe

If a pipe empties the tank or there is a continuous leak, its efficiency is taken as negative (−) while calculating the combined efficiency.

Combined Rate Formula

If two pipes A and B fill a tank in x and y hours respectively, the time taken to fill the tank together is given directly by (x × y) ÷ (x + y).
